text:
rachel: FYI the new Next/Edge sample we shipped is failing only when built for ESM + edge adapters. stack: \"TypeError: Class extends value undefined\". Node local server is fine.
rachel: Repro repo link pasted in thread and minimal build config below.
rachel: package.json snippet:
```
{
  \"name\": \"redwood-onboard-sample\",
  \"type\": \"module\",
  \"exports\": { \"import\": \"./dist/sdk.mjs\", \"require\": \"./dist/sdk.cjs\" }
}
```
rachel: tsconfig.json snippet:
```
{
  \"compilerOptions\": {
    \"target\": \"ES2020\",
    \"module\": \"ESNext\",
    \"moduleResolution\": \"bundler\",
    \"declaration\": true,
    \"isolatedModules\": true
  }
}
```
tom: bundlers sometimes rewrite conditional export wrappers and introduce a CJS shim that references globalThis fallbacks. That can break class prototypes if helpers are injected differently.
marco: do you have an example SDK export shape? is it using a conditional default export for CJS compatibility?
rachel: yes, SDK ships a small runtime shim: 
```
if (typeof exports === 'object') module.exports = require('./sdk.cjs');
else export default require('./sdk.mjs');
```
rachel: when the edge bundler inlines that shim it ends up with undefined and the subclassing blows up.
vishal: two pieces: runtime interop and authoring ergonomics. On runtime, simplest for edge samples is to publish/import only pure ESM artifacts. On types, using `unknown` in public generics hurts intellisense for JS users.
tom: agreed. For TS surface we should prefer `T = any` for backwards DX but keep strictness in internal APIs. Alternatively export small typed helpers: `client.asType<T>()` or `client.json<T>()` so callers can opt in.
marco: another tip: set moduleResolution to `node16` for samples that target bundlers that understand node-style exports. `bundler` can cause unexpected resolution rewrites.
rachel: i tried flipping esModuleInterop on, which made runtime fine but caused overload inference to degrade in our SDK tests. overloads with `unknown` vs `any` started failing CI type-checks.
vishal: for overloads: prefer overloads where the generic param has a default to unknown but also provide a non-generic overload returning `Record<string, any>` for untyped JS usage. e.g.
```
request(path: string, body?: any): Promise<Record<string, any>>;
request<T = unknown>(path: string, body?: unknown): Promise<T>;
```
marco: that pattern helps IDEs for vanilla JS while preserving strict typing for TS authors.
tom: also watch out for polyfills; the CJS shim in some build paths pulls in a small polyfill that references `self` which breaks in some edge runtimes. Removing CJS-only shims from edge sample eliminated that.
rachel: immediate plan: 1) change sample package.json to only import the ESM export, 2) change tsconfig.moduleResolution to node16 for the sample, 3) add tiny helpers (`.json` / `.raw`) to improve JS DX, 4) add smoke CI that runs the built sample in a local edge runtime (vercel dev).
vishal: sounds good. devx-bot can you create a ticket for the CI smoke test and assign to @rachel?
devx-bot: created issue #1256: "sample-ci: build ESM-only sample and run edge dev smoke" with labels devex/ci and priority/medium. Assigned to @rachel.
rachel: thanks. i'll open a PR with the export tweak + helper API and include a short example in the README that shows `await client.request<{embedding:number[]}>(...)` and the new `client.json` shorthand for JS users. will ping for reviews.
marco: please include a small test that asserts the exported class is constructible after the edge build. That test would have caught this earlier.
vishal: and add a changelog note: "samples: prefer ESM-only artifacts to avoid bundler CJS shims."
